item.title: AWS extends Trusted Identity Propagation to IAM Federation and Roles Anywhere
item.description:
AWS extends Trusted Identity Propagation to IAM Federation and Roles Anywhere

AWS has extended Trusted Identity Propagation (TIP) to support IAM federation and AWS IAM Roles Anywhere, enabling customers to grant access and audit activity based on the specific user or workload behind an IAM role.

🔍 Overview

Trusted Identity Propagation (TIP) carries the identity of a user or workload with each AWS request. This allows users to grant permissions to that specific user or workload and trace its actions in AWS CloudTrail. Previously, TIP was available only for users accessing AWS through AWS IAM Identity Center. The new extension makes TIP work for users and workloads that federate directly into IAM roles or use X.509 certificates to obtain AWS credentials, while also simplifying TIP usage with IAM Identity Center.

🧩 How it works

TIP addresses the gap where access control decisions apply to the role rather than the user, and CloudTrail attributes each action to the role session. By attaching identity context from a trusted source to the role session at credential issuance, TIP provides a stable reference for the user or workload behind each request. This context is immutable for the lifetime of the session and can include optional claims, such as a risk score or a CI/CD workflow name.

The identity context propagates through supported downstream requests:

  • Role Assumption: When a TIP session assumes another role, AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) carries the context into the new role session.
  • Forward Access Sessions (FAS): When an AWS service makes a downstream request on your behalf, FAS credentials carry the identity context.
  • Outbound Federation: With IAM outbound identity federation, the session can request a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) that carries identity context to an external service.

⚙️ Key details

AWS validates the source and attaches identity context through three primary paths:

Path Source of Identity Context Trusted Source Type
IAM Federation SAML assertion or OIDC token External SAML or OIDC Identity Providers (IdP)
IAM Identity Center Username received from identity source IAM Identity Center
IAM Roles Anywhere X.509 certificate X.509 certificates

TIP context propagates to a new role session only under specific boundary conditions:

  • The target role is in the account where the identity provider is configured.
  • The target role is in another account within the same AWS organization.

IAM policies evaluate this identity context to authorize requests, and AWS CloudTrail records it for auditing. For example, Amazon S3 bucket policies and AWS Lambda can utilize this context for access control and audit logging. The identity context is represented through context keys, including the aws:OriginIdentity/* namespace, which serves as the common namespace for identity information across all three paths.

#AWS #IAM #CloudSecurity #IdentityManagement #CloudTrail #DevSecOps

Source: Know the identity behind the role: Authorize and audit with trusted identity propagation | Amazon Web Services

item.title: OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation
item.description:
OpenAI Releases Codex Security for Vulnerability Detection and Remediation

OpenAI has released Codex Security, a toolset for finding, investigating, and fixing vulnerabilities in code. It provides security workflows accessible in Codex, a command-line interface, and a TypeScript SDK for automation.

🔍 Overview

Codex Security helps developers:

  • Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes
  • Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes
  • Draft SECURITY.md policies and save threat models for later review
  • Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against custom rubrics, and suggest owners from source and Git history
  • Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud

🧩 How It Works

Scan Types

  • Standard scans investigate code for vulnerabilities
  • Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return deduplicated findings
  • Scans use existing root and component SECURITY.md guidance
  • A completed scan saves a report and findings

Post-Scan Actions

  • Read the report for source evidence and exclusions
  • Request a patch or ask Codex to verify an existing fix
  • Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub
  • Export results as SARIF, JSON, or CSV

⚙️ Key Details

Installation & Requirements

Component Requirement
Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or 24.x, or 26.x
Python 3.10+ (Python 3.10 also requires tomli)

CLI Usage

  • cs and codex-security run the same CLI
  • Use npx @openai/codex-security to skip global install or resolve EEXIST conflicts
  • Run cs scan . --max-time 15 for a 15-minute Standard investigation allowance
  • Use bulk scans for independent repository reviews in one resumable campaign
  • When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the REPORT path in the terminal
  • Run cs scans show from the same repository to find its latest completed scan

CI Configuration

  • Set OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY in the scan process’s environment

🔗 Integrations & Automation

  • Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and containers
  • Publish completed scans to Codex Security Cloud (optional; local scans work without it)
  • When Codex Security Cloud is available, the Security plugin’s $cloud-findings skill reads findings, reports, recorded assignment and verification, and scan status in Codex desktop or the Codex CLI
  • Linked Git worktrees share scan history and saved findings when they use the same Codex Security state directory
  • Keep CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR stable to retain shared history and sign-in scope

🔐 Advanced Features & Access Programs

  • Some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require Trusted Access for Cyber
  • For accounts with Daybreak access:
    • See Daybreak opt-in for the Codex toggle
    • See Cyber access programs to select a program explicitly
  • The SDK guide includes deep-scan configuration, validation, severity classification, owner suggestions, and result handling
  • Use policy to draft a new SECURITY.md or update an existing one

#OpenAI #CodexSecurity #DevSecOps #VulnerabilityScanning #AItools #CLI

Source: openai/codex-security

item.title: ToolHive: An enterprise platform for managing Model Context Protocol servers
item.description:
ToolHive: An enterprise platform for managing Model Context Protocol servers

ToolHive is an enterprise-grade platform designed for running and managing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. It allows organizations to run any MCP server securely, instantly, and anywhere, addressing the need for secure and observable MCP infrastructure in production environments.

🔍 Overview

ToolHive addresses the challenges of managing MCP servers by providing a modular architecture that streamlines secure server management and integration. Unlike most MCP solutions that are SaaS-based, ToolHive allows companies to self-host their MCP registry and gateway, which is particularly useful when compliance requirements prohibit sensitive information from being processed by SaaS providers. The platform includes a Kubernetes operator, enabling teams to declare policies and integrate with identity and observability stacks using familiar tools and patterns.

🧩 How it works

At its core, ToolHive wraps every MCP server in an isolated container with a minimal permission file that does not include local credentials. This isolation helps enforce security standards. The platform uses semantic tool search to reduce token usage by up to 85%. When configured with an authentication source, ToolHive enforces identity and access policy per request, giving platform teams the observability required for production environments. It also provides audit logs and configurable identity enforcement to address security concerns regarding shadow MCP use by developers.

⚙️ Key details

The platform offers a range of features for managing MCP infrastructure, including:

  • Defining dedicated endpoints for secure and efficient team access to tools
  • Orchestrating multiple tools into a virtual MCP using a deterministic workflow engine
  • Centralizing control of security policy, authentication, authorization, and auditing
  • Integrating with Identity Providers (IdP) for Single Sign-On (SSO) via OIDC/OAuth compatibility
  • Customizing and filtering tools and descriptions to improve performance and reduce token usage
  • Connecting with local clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and VS Code Server
  • Curating a catalog of trusted servers for quick discovery and deployment
  • Integrating with the official MCP registry and adding custom MCP servers
  • Grouping servers based on role or use case
  • Managing the registry via an API-driven interface or embedding it in existing workflows
  • Verifying provenance and signing servers with built-in security controls
  • Providing preset configurations and permissions for a frictionless user experience

🚀 Availability

ToolHive supports flexible deployment options to suit different organizational needs. Users can deploy MCP servers in the cloud via Kubernetes for enterprise scalability, or run them locally via Docker or Podman. Additionally, the platform can proxy remote MCP servers securely for unified management. Organizations can pilot the entire platform and, when ready to scale, leverage Stacklok’s added capabilities and expert team support.

#ToolHive #MCP #Kubernetes #EnterpriseAI #DevSecOps

Source: stacklok/toolhive

item.title: Argus AI Security Platform Launches with Self-Hosted Multi-Tenant Capabilities
item.description:
Argus AI Security Platform Launches with Self-Hosted Multi-Tenant Capabilities

A new self-hosted, multi-tenant, and MIT-licensed security platform named Argus has been released to watch cloud, identity, code, endpoints, network, and Kubernetes environments.

🔍 Overview

Argus catches attacks at machine speed, investigates them with AI agents, and contains them in seconds. The platform operates offline for air-gapped installs and ensures security data never leaves the user’s hands.

🧩 How it works

  • Nine specialist agents triage, investigate, and hunt using read-only tools.
  • Agents can propose a fix but never execute one; their one write-capable tool creates a pending request.
  • Everything agents read is treated as untrusted data so prompt injections become signals instead of hijacks.
  • Autonomous response playbooks act the moment a detection fires using a catalog of 27 typed actions.
  • Every autonomous feature ships off by default so users can enable autonomy gradually.

⚙️ Key details

  • AI Gateway: Puts OpenAI and Anthropic traffic behind org-held keys, model allowlists, data-loss prevention, prompt-injection flags, and budgets.
  • Shadow-AI Discovery: Finds services used without approval via network, cloud, and SSO telemetry.
  • Canaries: Built for agents with hidden prompt injections, agent rules files, a fake MCP server, and fake LLM API keys.
  • Attack Simulator: Replays eight AI-driven attack scenarios in an isolated sandbox tenant.
  • Pentesting: Autopilot and native autonomous pentesting plan tests and run them through a scope-checked harness.
  • Vulnerability Enrichment: CVE findings are enriched with CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list and EPSS scores, automatically raising severity.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployment options include Docker Compose for pilots, Helm for Kubernetes, and Terraform for AWS and Azure.
  • Encrypted backups run on a schedule and land on disk, S3, or Azure with single-command restore and verification checks.
  • Control mappings for SOC 2, NIST 800-171, and ISO 27001 are included.

#AISecurity #AIAgents #Cybersecurity #DevSecOps #CloudSecurity

Source: thomasunise/argus

item.title: Prowler Brings AI to Open Source Cloud Security Platform
item.description:
Prowler Brings AI to Open Source Cloud Security Platform

Prowler, the world’s most widely used open-source cloud security platform, now includes AI-driven capabilities to automate security and compliance across any cloud environment. This update positions Prowler as a platform that can “Secure ANY Cloud at AI Speed,” offering thousands of ready-to-use security checks and compliance frameworks.

🔍 Overview

Prowler is the Open Cloud Security Platform trusted by thousands to automate security and compliance in any cloud environment. With thousands of ready-to-use checks and compliance frameworks, Prowler delivers real-time, customizable monitoring and seamless integrations, making cloud security simple, scalable, and cost-effective for organizations of any size.

⚙️ Key Capabilities

Prowler now delivers AI-driven, customizable, and easy-to-use assessments, dashboards, reports, and integrations, making cloud security simple, scalable, and cost-effective for organizations of any size. Key features include:

  • Thousands of ready-to-use security checks, remediation guidance, and compliance frameworks
  • Prowler ThreatScore: Weighted risk prioritization scoring that helps you focus on the most critical security findings first

🏆 Supported Compliance Frameworks

Prowler includes hundreds of built-in controls to ensure compliance with a wide range of standards and frameworks:

Category Frameworks
Industry Standards CIS, NIST 800, NIST CSF, CISA, and MITRE ATT&CK
Regulatory Compliance and Governance RBI, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, and NIS2
Frameworks for Sensitive Data and Privacy GDPR, HIPAA, and FFIEC
Organizational Governance and Quality Control SOC2, GXP, and ISO 27001
Cloud-Specific Frameworks AWS Foundational Technical Review (FTR), AWS Well-Architected Framework, and BSI C5
National Security Standards ENS (Spanish National Security Scheme) and KISA ISMS-P (Korean)
Custom Security Frameworks Tailored to your needs

🚀 Availability

Prowler is available in two web application formats that simplify running Prowler across your cloud provider accounts:

  • Prowler Cloud: A hosted web application
  • Prowler Local Server: A self-hosted open-source version

Both provide a user-friendly interface to visualize the results and streamline your security assessments. For more details, refer to the Prowler Local Server documentation and try Prowler Cloud.

💡 Why It Matters

By integrating AI-driven assessments and threat prioritization into an open-source platform with thousands of built-in checks and extensive compliance framework support, Prowler makes cloud security more accessible and efficient for organizations of any size. The community is invited to join the Prowler community.

#OpenSource #CloudSecurity #AI #Compliance #DevSecOps #Prowler

Source: prowler-cloud/prowler
